name: Justicia

project_scope.note: Two historical/source-pool Justicia names resolve to two different accepted genera. This is a genus recognition lesson with a family-linked historical-name comparison, not a claim that both are accepted Justicia.

look_here_first: For J. pilosella, look for a very low, hairy dry-site perennial with small opposite ciliate leaves and paired axillary flowers. A tall, nearly glabrous colony along shallow water with narrow leaves and long-peduncled flower spikes is Dianthera americana (historically Justicia americana).
shared_genus_traits: Current canonical J. pilosella belongs to Acanthaceae: opposite simple leaves, bilateral tubular flowers and a capsule with seed-support structures.
Two fertile stamens and anther architecture help route specimens toward Justicia-like Acanthaceae, but are not a complete species key.
The historical name Justicia americana must be resolved to accepted Dianthera americana before teaching genus membership.

quick_identification_steps: Locate mature leaf nodes and flower placement, not flower color.
Low, hairy and small-leaved with paired axillary flowers: follow canonical Justicia pilosella.
Tall, rhizomatous and nearly glabrous at water edge with peduncled spikes: follow canonical Dianthera americana.
Confirm with capsule/seed supports when available; avoid hard keys based only on habitat.
overlap_and_cautions: Both may have opposite leaves and tubular bilateral flowers; those characters identify the family neighborhood rather than the species.
The Master Plant Pool retains Justicia americana, but GitHub correctly places its accepted concept in Dianthera; do not create a duplicate Justicia americana species page.
Both canonical records retain unresolved target-zone native status and are learner-approved; do not convert either to PASS.
Do not treat habitat alone as definitive; examine stems, leaf hairs, inflorescence structure and fruits.

local_lookalikes.separator: Often showier solitary or few tubular flowers; examine capsule, calyx and retinacula, not corolla color.
Compare small opposite leaves, calyx and mature capsule; don't confuse generic Acanthaceae traits with Justicia diagnosis.
Usually woody shrubs with slender tubular flowers; compare branch habit, flower position and anthers.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: J. pilosella whole low mound with scale, matched against D. americana water-edge colony.
Both taxa: entire opposite leaf and node, plus hair/ciliate-margin macro at same magnification.
J. pilosella paired axillary flowers versus D. americana peduncled flower spike, showing attachment to stem.
Both taxa: flower profile and stamen/anther close-up; label structures.
Both taxa: opened mature capsule, seeds and any retinacula, with millimeter scale.
